What you get

Six things that change
for your practice.

Most of what erodes a design happens after the drawings leave your office. Here is how we stop it.

Your design

Your design intent survives construction

Reveals, alignments and ceiling heights are resolved in the model before work starts, so nobody improvises them on site.

HowModeled and coordinated in Revit first.

Your budget

Real cost feedback while you are still designing

Cost ranges come straight from the model as you draw, so you design to the budget instead of being cut back to it later.

HowOpen-book cost-plus, every line visible.

Your authority

No value engineering behind your back

When something has to change, you and the owner see the priced options first. You stay the author of the design.

HowEvery change routed to you with its cost.

Your time

Less construction administration

Conflicts are solved on screen, not on site. Fewer visits, more time to design.

HowCoordinated in the model before CDs are issued.

Your client

Approvals that stick

The owner walks the lit house before it is built. Decisions are made once.

HowPhotoreal walkthroughs with real lighting.

Your portfolio

A finished space that matches your renderings

The project you publish is the one you designed.

HowShop drawings checked before fabrication.
